solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Turn over to clean small herring fillets

parts.note: to roll is to turn over
to mop is to clean a floor
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An instruction for preparing fish: flip the fillets, then wash them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollmops are pickled herring fillets rolled around a filling, a dish from Germany.

clue.text: Missing opening, cannon section ring and reverberate

indicators.note: missing its opening means the first letter of the word for the cannon part is dropped

parts.note: the breech is the rear part of a cannon barrel, where it is loaded
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A cannon's damaged part rings out with a booming echo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing opening' takes the B off BREECH to leave REECH.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-echo is to sound back again and again, which is what reverberating does.

clue.text: Can family together make a short visit?

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is loo
kin are your family

explanation.surface: A question about whether relatives can pop round together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the slang noun for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To look in on someone is to drop by briefly, a short call.

clue.text: Gets wrong idea about notes on book

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale, so two or more of them are mis
Judges is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone misreads the annotations written on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To misjudge is to form a mistaken opinion of someone or something.

clue.text: Set of advisers under throne?

parts.note: the body advising the monarch serves under the throne; but 'throne' is also slang for a toilet, or privy, and the advisers sit beneath that word

explanation.surface: A description of the monarch's councillors serving beneath the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Privy Council is the formal body of advisers to the British sovereign; 'throne' also means a lavatory, which is another sense of privy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Privy Council is a group of senior counsellors who formally advise the British monarch.

clue.text: Unhappy about page on the subject of food

indicators.note: about means the word for unhappy goes round the other pieces

parts.note: unhappy means sad
re means concerning, on the subject of

explanation.surface: A miserable page of writing about food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the container signal; 'on the subject of' does that job instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is food smeared on bread, such as jam or paste; also a lavish meal.

clue.text: Joanna's rather too good with a "no"

definitions.note: Joanna's here is Joanna is, with the 's as link to the wordplay; Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for the instrument

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious, rather too good

explanation.surface: A woman named Joanna is a goody-goody who keeps saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang (from 'pianner'), a London way of naming the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a joanna is the keyboard instrument found in pubs.

clue.text: Checked fabric cut on the reverse

indicators.note: on the reverse means the combined fabric and cutting words are read backwards

parts.note: denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone inspected cloth trimmed on its back side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the reverse' turns DENIMAXE around.
explanation.definitionFit: To have examined something is to have checked or inspected it.

clue.text: Wind movements tug Shard all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Gusts make a tug boat and London's Shard tower seem to sway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shard is a very tall skyscraper in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts are currents of air, movements of wind through a room.

clue.text: Thinking of oneself having work in bustling cities

indicators.note: in means the word for work sits inside the rearranged letters
bustling suggests energetic movement, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: go means work, function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A self-centred person working in busy cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is the verb sense, as a machine works or goes; 'bustling' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoistic person is self-absorbed, concerned mainly with their own interests.

clue.text: Mum and gran are coming together tomorrow

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
nana is an informal word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Mother and grandmother will be visiting the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, borrowed into English for some vague later time.

clue.text: Crack low-tech cuckoo for very precise timekeeper

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fix a basic cuckoo clock to make it an accurate timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the clock but is the anagram signal; the definition is playful, since a clock-watcher keeps a very close eye on the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-watcher is a worker who constantly checks the time, waiting to leave, so jokingly a precise timekeeper.

clue.text: Followers of every line of Anouilh play like folksy and lusty poetry

parts.note: the letter following L in Anouilh is H
the letter following L in play is A
the letter following L in like is I
the letter following L in folksy is K
the letter following L in lusty is U

explanation.surface: Describing verse by Anouilh as folksy and lusty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' stands for the letter L: the letter after L in anouiLH, pLAy, LIke, foLKsy and LUsty gives H, A, I, K, U. Jean Anouilh was a French playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese verse form of three lines, so a piece of poetry.

clue.text: Cry, being unsettled and showing signs of advancing years

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
owing means still to be paid, as an unsettled bill is

explanation.surface: Someone crying out, upset and visibly getting old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' suggests agitation but means a debt not yet paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper and teeth go yellow with age, so yellowing shows that something is ageing.

clue.text: A majority of sexual partners?

parts.note: majority here means legal adulthood, the age at which partners may lawfully have sex, not most of them

explanation.surface: A question about most of someone's lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' reads as 'most' but is the legal coming of age.
explanation.definitionFit: The age at which a person may lawfully agree to sexual activity is the legal threshold for partners.

clue.text: Fruit — a number outside crate getting spoiled

indicators.note: outside means the number goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: nine is a number

indicators.note: getting spoiled means the letters of crate are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit packed around a crate that is going bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoiled crate letters sit inside the number after its first letter, signalled by 'outside'; 'a' belongs with 'number'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Friendly chat with head of security about Her Majesty and leak

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to ooze is to leak slowly

explanation.surface: A security chief chats about the Queen and a leaked secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To schmooze is to chat in a friendly, ingratiating way; as a noun it is such talk.

clue.text: Successful pickpocket, one often seen at village fete

definitions.text: one often seen at village fete

parts.note: lucky means fortunate, successful
dip is slang for a pickpocket

explanation.surface: A thief has a good day working the crowd at a village fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A lucky dip is a British fair stall where you pull an unseen prize from a tub; a fete is a local outdoor fundraising fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky dips are a classic stall at village fetes, a game of chance with wrapped prizes.

clue.text: Something for consumers — suit with western isle check

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in cards
and means together with
I is the abbreviation for isle or island
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A shopper's guide to suits and a check-patterned jacket from a western island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumers' suggests shoppers but means eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A club sandwich is a triple-decker sandwich, something made to be eaten.

clue.text: Flying visit introducing British musician

indicators.note: introducing means the rearranged visit letters take in the abbreviation
flying means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quick trip featuring a British musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' turns VISIT into VIIST, and 'introducing' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibist plays the vibraphone, so is a musician.

clue.text: Question silver head in guessing answer: old zebra?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: head in means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A quiz question about an extinct zebra, answered by guesswork.
explanation.definitionFit: The quagga was a South African zebra relative with stripes only at the front, extinct since 1883.

clue.text: Interim move?

definitions.meaning: a temporary stopgap, used for the time being
read as two words, to ... is an old phrase for managing or getting by, to shift oneself

explanation.surface: A short query about a stopgap step.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift serves for now until a proper one comes, so it is temporary.

clue.text: An end to this callous contempt

indicators.note: an end to means the last letter of the following word

parts.note: a corn is a callus, a hard patch of skin; callous is used as a noun spelling here

explanation.surface: A plea to stop this heartless disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'callous' reads as heartless but is taken as a hardened patch of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn is open disdain or contempt for someone thought unworthy.

clue.text: All the best go west, getting into gold

indicators.note: getting into means the phrase for dying goes inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to go west is an idiom for to die

explanation.surface: Good wishes to someone heading west to find gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, said like 'all the best' when parting.

clue.text: Pretty likely old theologian gets what Christ was to God

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
Christ is the Son of God

explanation.surface: An elderly theologian grasps the relation of Christ to God.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is odds-on is the favourite, so its winning is fairly probable.

clue.text: Making fast brew at home in gallons

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, a brew
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Brewing up a large quantity at home quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' suggests speed but means secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaining something secures it firmly in place, making it fixed.

clue.text: Use editor to introduce unknown writer

indicators.note: to introduce means the editor takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: X is the algebraic unknown
a pen is a writer, something that writes

explanation.surface: Get an editor to present an anonymous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown writer' suggests an obscure author but gives X and PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To expend is to use up resources or energy.

clue.text: Immature wood cut for infusion

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced

indicators.note: cut means the word for the wood loses its last letter

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Young timber is chopped to brew a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks TEAK to TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is made by steeping unfermented leaves in hot water, an infusion.
